key_insight: Directed Social Regard is a representation and model that detects and attributes coexisting pro- and anti-social intents (e.g., advocacy, aid, opposition, harm, victimization) to specific targets within the same message, revealing nuanced directed social behaviors that aggregate sentiment scores miss.
problem_solved: Existing sentiment tools provide an overall polarity but cannot identify multiple, opposing social intents directed at different targets in one text, limiting detection of targeted advocacy, harm, aid, or victimization in online media.
method: Define an annotation schema for Directed Social Regard: label social action categories (advocacy, opposition, aid, harm, victimization) plus directionality toward identified target spans.
Create and annotate a dataset drawn from online media / influence operations and train a model that jointly extracts target spans and predicts multi-label, target-directed social actions.
Evaluate against sentiment baselines and ablations to demonstrate improved detection of mixed/opposing sentiments and target-specific harms/aid signals.
impact: Provides ML practitioners with a practical framework and data to build systems that recognize mixed, target-directed social behavior rather than coarse global sentiment — improving content moderation, harm detection, influence analysis, and social media research.

paper_title: Directed Social Regard: Surfacing Targeted Advocacy, Opposition, Aid, Harms, and Victimization in Online Media
paper_authors: Scott Friedman, Ruta Wheelock, Sonja Schmer-Galunder, Drisana Iverson, Jake Vasilakes
